label: GO-only; grows with recent unrewarded a2 trials and S2-leaning belief
terms: (phase == GO) * (prev_action == 2) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (tv("action", -2) == 2) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * np.clip(-belief_lo, -4, 4) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 0) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a2 S1 r") ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a1 S1 u")
explanation: Active only at GO (timing baseline rises over the episode; D1/D2 are zero). Beyond timing the magnitude behaves like an accumulator of unrewarded a2 choices: +1.06 if the last trial was a2 unrewarded (either state), +0.46 more if the trial before was also a2 unrewarded, +0.66 for two unrewarded trials in a row (any choice); a reward on the last trial lowers it (-0.44), most after a2 S1 rewarded (extra -0.49), and a1 S1 unrewarded also lowers it (-0.31). Ideal-observer belief that S2 is good (-belief_lo, clipped) adds a graded positive term (+0.13 per log-odds unit). Observed-only, 7 terms: dev R^2 beyond timing 0.655, test 0.644, against an all-observed ceiling of 0.67 and an all ceiling of 0.68, so leaving out the model value/policy and the future choice costs little (the earlier firing label leaned on the upcoming a2 choice; trial history plus belief recovers this). Residual misses: under-predicted on the first trial of a window (history unknown; adding prev_action == -1 gives dev 0.668), and the longest no-reward a2 streaks, where activation saturates near 5. Future variables not used.

issues: I could not refute it. The 7 terms reproduce test R^2 beyond timing 0.644, against an all-observed ceiling of 0.67 and an 'all' ceiling of 0.68. The fitted weights match the explanation: +1.06, +0.46, -0.44, +0.13, +0.66, -0.49, -0.31.
The belief term is needed. Dropping it lowers test R^2 from 0.644 to 0.523, and belief alone scores 0.187. The S2-leaning part of the label holds up.

Calling it a 'counter of unrewarded a2' overstates things slightly. The +0.66 two-unrewarded-in-a-row term applies to either choice. Going back a third trial (a three-trial a2 unrewarded streak) adds nothing on test (0.659 with or without it), so the count only reaches back two trials.

Systematic misses are small. GO on the first trial of a window (history unknown) is under-predicted by +0.24, and GO after a1 S2 r by +0.17. A prev_action == -1 term raises test R^2 to 0.659, and adding belief x prev_reward==0 gives 0.661. The 'saturates near 5' misses are long a2 streaks that the additive terms under-predict, as the explanation already says.
The profile confirms the feature is GO-only: the D1 and D2 residuals are about 0. No future variables are used.
